# CODINGVAULT (inherits the root runtime + NEXUS; code lives here)

The loop, tiering, delegation, verification, and ship mechanics come from the root layer and
skills. This file adds only what is code-vault-specific: the hard invariants and the playbooks.
A project's own `.claude/` overrides everything here EXCEPT I0.

Memory and persistence are default behavior here too: `agentdb recall` first, commission per
logical unit, chronicle at the end, lesson learned to agentdb. No code-vault exemption.

## Subagent routing

Model, effort, and prompt are the dispatching agent's call, made per task. Start from the working
recommendation in `Vaults/_meta/reference/coordination/model-routing.md` (never route cold, never
route by prestige), then decide and state your pick in one line. Cross-harness mechanics
(codex-lane.sh, traced_claude) live in
`Vaults/_meta/reference/coordination/multi-agent-coordination.md`. High-consequence builders never
grade their own work; use a fresh independent verifier.

## I0. Invariants (violation = stop, regroup, redo)

- **I0.1** Commit before move: never `mv`/`rm` in `_meta/` without committing first.
  Untracked = unrecoverable. New `_meta/` file → commit immediately.
- **I0.4** No AI attribution on commits: no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated with", ever.
- **I0.5** Never `--no-verify`; fix the gate. Sole machine carve-out: the kernel plugin's
  `session-end.sh` + `pre-compact-commit.sh` (verify would re-invoke the hook chain).
- **I0.6** Subagents report; the main agent commits. Sole carve-out: a landing lane explicitly
  dispatched to commit (e.g. burn-lander, or a prompt that grants it in so many words). Everyone
  else: report, never `git commit`.
- **I0.7** Frontend: no Inter, no emoji, no generic AI aesthetic (`kernel:frontend`).
- **I0.8** Push immediately after every commit, including main (root ship mechanics). Only
  exception: a deliberately throwaway branch, stated out loud.
- **I0.8b** **Done means MERGED INTO THE DEFAULT BRANCH.** Not committed, not pushed, not "on a
  branch", not "PR opened". Work that ends on a feature branch has shipped nothing, however green
  its tests are, and must never be reported as a completed deliverable. Before saying a thing is
  done, run `git log --oneline origin/<default>..HEAD` and confirm it is empty. If a merge is
  genuinely blocked, name the blocker in the same breath as reporting the work, and leave the
  branch named in the handoff so it cannot be silently lost.
- **I0.9** No secrets in tree, logs, or commit messages. `.env*` / `.envrc` / `.mcp.json`
  gitignored. Leak → rotate + scrub.
- **I0.10/11** Every spawn contract names allowed tools + file globs; sensitive scopes
  (auth, payments, PII, secrets) get explicit capability limits, default-deny destructive/
  network/credential access.
- **I0.12** No hallucinated APIs: an external call you haven't grepped in-repo resolves
  through installed package source or official docs before you write it.
- **I0.13** Anchor-drift = stop, `kernel:handoff`, `/clear`. Triggers: repeated failed gate,
  patch churn, 3 low-information replies, user signal. Self-detection is unreliable; accept
  external triggers.
- **I0.14** **No worktrees for agent work.** Never create one to give yourself a private tree;
  work inline on the current branch. If work genuinely cannot share a tree, stop and get a
  decision first.
  **One scoped exception, granted by Aria 2026-08-25:** the issue-pipeline runner
  (`_meta/services/issue-pipeline/dispatch.sh`) creates a throwaway worktree per lane, precisely
  so it never has to touch a working tree it did not create. That is the opposite of the failure
  this rule guards: it exists because `our4cuts` carried 57 of Aria's uncommitted files through
  13 automated lanes and had to come out byte-identical. The runner removes each worktree in a
  trap and `git worktree prune`s on startup. Any other use still needs a decision first.
- **I0.15** Critical safety (destructive commands, secrets, push protection) is enforced by
  hooks, not honor-system. The agent cannot bypass its own rules; the hook can.
- **I0.16** Artifact-first output. A requested reply, explanation, draft, report, review,
  plan, brief, or other substantive deliverable is a document in the requested format and
  location. If unstated, use the nearest project convention, then a clearly named durable
  file near the work. Never replace it with long chat or terminal text. Chat only gives the
  exact path and a few verification facts. If uncertain whether a file is wanted, create it.

## Code playbooks (the non-generic parts)

- **Bug fix:** reproduce first (can't reproduce → can't fix); grep siblings and root-cause
  the CLASS, not the symptom; patch all siblings in this change or write survivors to
  `_meta/plans/<bug>.md`; regression test fails-before/passes-after.
- **Feature:** failures-first research map in `_meta/research/<topic>.md` before non-trivial
  builds (spawn `kernel:deep-diver`); search-first, a close match within the same ownership
  boundary gets extended, never forked; smallest viable change; if a fix would repeat on the
  next file, promote to a shared module now.
- **Bulk mechanical (rename/migrate/regenerate N things):** commit a clean baseline FIRST,
  script it (deterministic beats agentic), dry-run on 1-2 files, inspect the diff, then run
  the full set. Subagents only when a script is genuinely impossible.
- **Refactor:** full sweep audit before touching anything; behavior-preserving only (tests
  green before AND after); the file ends shorter or no longer; commit per logical step.
- **Data migration:** backup + record the path in the commit; idempotent by construction;
  dry-run on fixtures with row counts before/after; rollback path written BEFORE any
